1  """
   2  This module implements tables, the central place for accessing and manipulating
   3  data in TinyDB.
   4  """
   5  
   6  from collections.abc import Callable, Iterable, Iterator, Mapping, MutableMapping
   7  from typing import (
   8      NoReturn,
   9      Optional,
  10      Union,
  11      cast,
  12      overload
  13  )
  14  
  15  from .queries import QueryLike
  16  from .storages import Storage
  17  from .utils import LRUCache
  18  
  19  __all__ = ('Document', 'Table')
  20  
  21  
  22  class Document(dict):
  23      """
  24      A document stored in the database.
  25  
  26      This class provides a way to access both a document's content and
  27      its ID using ``doc.doc_id``.
  28      """
  29  
  30      def __init__(self, value: Mapping, doc_id: int):
  31          super().__init__(value)
  32          self.doc_id = doc_id
  33  
  34  
  35  class Table:
  36      """
  37      Represents a single TinyDB table.
  38  
  39      It provides methods for accessing and manipulating documents.
  40  
  41      .. admonition:: Query Cache
  42  
  43          As an optimization, a query cache is implemented using a
  44          :class:`~tinydb.utils.LRUCache`. This class mimics the interface of
  45          a normal ``dict``, but starts to remove the least-recently used entries
  46          once a threshold is reached.
  47  
  48          The query cache is updated on every search operation. When writing
  49          data, the whole cache is discarded as the query results may have
  50          changed.
  51  
  52      .. admonition:: Customization
  53  
  54          For customization, the following class variables can be set:
  55  
  56          - ``document_class`` defines the class that is used to represent
  57            documents,
  58          - ``document_id_class`` defines the class that is used to represent
  59            document IDs,
  60          - ``query_cache_class`` defines the class that is used for the query
  61            cache
  62          - ``default_query_cache_capacity`` defines the default capacity of
  63            the query cache
  64  
  65          .. versionadded:: 4.0
  66  
  67  
  68      :param storage: The storage instance to use for this table
  69      :param name: The table name
  70      :param cache_size: Maximum capacity of query cache
  71      :param persist_empty: Store new table even with no operations on it
  72      """
  73  
  74      #: The class used to represent documents
  75      #:
  76      #: .. versionadded:: 4.0
  77      document_class = Document
  78  
  79      #: The class used to represent a document ID
  80      #:
  81      #: .. versionadded:: 4.0
  82      document_id_class = int
  83  
  84      #: The class used for caching query results
  85      #:
  86      #: .. versionadded:: 4.0
  87      query_cache_class = LRUCache
  88  
  89      #: The default capacity of the query cache
  90      #:
  91      #: .. versionadded:: 4.0
  92      default_query_cache_capacity = 10
  93  
  94      def __init__(
  95          self,
  96          storage: Storage,
  97          name: str,
  98          cache_size: int = default_query_cache_capacity,
  99          persist_empty: bool = False
 100      ):
 101          """
 102          Create a table instance.
 103          """
 104  
 105          self._storage = storage
 106          self._name = name
 107          self._query_cache: LRUCache[QueryLike, list[Document]] \
 108              = self.query_cache_class(capacity=cache_size)
 109  
 110          self._next_id: Optional[int] = None
 111          # Only persist a brand-new empty table. Never clear existing documents
 112          # when reopen/construct with persist_empty=True (see issue #636).
 113          if persist_empty and not self._read_table():
 114              self._update_table(lambda table: table.clear())
 115  
 116      def __repr__(self):
 117          args = [
 118              'name={!r}'.format(self.name),
 119              'total={}'.format(len(self)),
 120              'storage={}'.format(self._storage),
 121          ]
 122  
 123          return '<{} {}>'.format(type(self).__name__, ', '.join(args))
 124  
 125      @property
 126      def name(self) -> str:
 127          """
 128          Get the table name.
 129          """
 130          return self._name
 131  
 132      @property
 133      def storage(self) -> Storage:
 134          """
 135          Get the table storage instance.
 136          """
 137          return self._storage
 138  
 139      def insert(self, document: Mapping) -> int:
 140          """
 141          Insert a new document into the table.
 142  
 143          :param document: the document to insert
 144          :returns: the inserted document's ID
 145          """
 146  
 147          # Make sure the document implements the ``Mapping`` interface
 148          if not isinstance(document, Mapping):
 149              raise ValueError('Document is not a Mapping')
 150  
 151          # First, we get the document ID for the new document
 152          if isinstance(document, self.document_class):
 153              # For a `Document` object we use the specified ID
 154              doc_id = document.doc_id
 155  
 156              # We also reset the stored next ID so the next insert won't
 157              # re-use document IDs by accident when storing an old value
 158              self._next_id = None
 159          else:
 160              # In all other cases we use the next free ID
 161              doc_id = self._get_next_id()
 162  
 163          # Now, we update the table and add the document
 164          def updater(table: dict):
 165              if doc_id in table:
 166                  raise ValueError(f'Document with ID {str(doc_id)} '
 167                                   f'already exists')
 168  
 169              # By calling ``dict(document)`` we convert the data we got to a
 170              # ``dict`` instance even if it was a different class that
 171              # implemented the ``Mapping`` interface
 172              table[doc_id] = dict(document)
 173  
 174          # See below for details on ``Table._update``
 175          self._update_table(updater)
 176  
 177          return doc_id
 178  
 179      def insert_multiple(self, documents: Iterable[Mapping]) -> list[int]:
 180          """
 181          Insert multiple documents into the table.
 182  
 183          :param documents: an Iterable of documents to insert
 184          :returns: a list containing the inserted documents' IDs
 185          """
 186          doc_ids = []
 187  
 188          def updater(table: dict):
 189              for document in documents:
 190  
 191                  # Make sure the document implements the ``Mapping`` interface
 192                  if not isinstance(document, Mapping):
 193                      raise ValueError('Document is not a Mapping')
 194  
 195                  if isinstance(document, self.document_class):
 196                      # Check if document does not override an existing document
 197                      if document.doc_id in table:
 198                          raise ValueError(
 199                              f'Document with ID {str(document.doc_id)} '
 200                              f'already exists'
 201                          )
 202  
 203                      # Store the doc_id, so we can return all document IDs
 204                      # later. Then save the document with its doc_id and
 205                      # skip the rest of the current loop
 206                      doc_id = document.doc_id
 207                      doc_ids.append(doc_id)
 208                      table[doc_id] = dict(document)
 209                      # Same as insert(): don't reuse this ID for later
 210                      # auto-assigned documents in this batch.
 211                      self._next_id = None
 212                      continue
